newsitem.title: USA: Dow ekes out record, Microsoft sparks tech rally.
newsitem.headline: Dow ekes out record, Microsoft sparks tech rally.

text.p: Wall Street stocks resumed their record-setting run on Monday, as strong earnings from Microsoft Corp sparked a broad technology rally that helped lift the Dow industrials to yet another record.

The Dow rose 11 points to close unofficially at 6844, its ninth all-time high of the young year. Even with the record, the Dow was no match for the tech-laden Nasdaq Composite, which surged 15 points to 1364.

Nasdaq's closing mark also represented a new all-time high, the index's sixth this year. Shares in Microsoft, which reported stronger than expected second quarter results following last Friday's close, jumped 3-5/8 to 90-3/4.

"The market looked at Microsoft's numbers and said the underlying fundamentals in technology are still intact," said Arnie Owen, director of equities at Kaufman Brothers. "Technology is still the driver."
Outside the technology sector trading was more tentative in part because the bond market closed in observance of the Martin Luther King Jr holiday.
Also looming is an appearance tomorrow before the U.S. Senate by Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan.

Comments by Greenspan, always carefully scrutinized for any clue about Fed policy, are a persistent source of tension for markets. With the outcome of the Fed's next policy meeting still a metter of debate, the comments are drawing even sharper attention.
"If he's really planning a tightening I think there will be a hint to the Senate tomorrow," said Edgar Peters, chief investment strategist at PanAgora Asset Management Inc.
Most economists expect no rate change at the next Fed meeting but some see sufficient cause in recent employment and other data for the Fed to make a pre-emptive strike against incipient inflation.

Absent a signal on the interest rate front, earnings will likely continue to dominate investor attention. Among the companies due to report tomorrow are International Business Machines Corp and U.S. banking giants Citicorp and Chase Manhattan Corp.
Bank stocks were among the busiest issues after Banc One Corp agreed to a $7.3 billion stock swap deal to acquire First USA Inc, a leading credit card issuer.
Shares in First USA soared 8-7/8 to 45-5/8 on the news, while Banc One slipped 3-1/2 to 41-5/8.

The deal sparked interest in other leading card issuers. Among the strongest were MBNA Corp, up 2-3/8 to 33-1/2, Capital One Financial Corp, up 4-7/8 to 38-3/8 and Advanta Corp, up 5-9/16 to 48-11/16.
Target Therapeutics Inc surged 10-1/4 to 57 on speculation the company would be acquired by Boston Scientific Corp a deal that was confirmed after the close of trading.
Shares in Boston Scientific, which will pay 1.07 shares for each Target share, fell 4-5/8 to 66-7/8 ahead of the announcement.

Broad market indicators reflected the market's cautious attitude. Advancing and declining issues ran in a virtual dead heat and the New York Stock Exchange Composite closed unchanged at 409.31. The S&P 500 rose 0.53 to a record 776.70.
